SEARCH
Package org.aeonbits.owner

Annotation Type Config.DeclaredOnly

Enclosing interface:
Config
@Retention(RUNTIME) @Target(TYPE) @Documented public static @interface Config.DeclaredOnly
Shows, through Accessible and Object.toString(), only the properties this interface declares.

One file read by several mapping interfaces is an ordinary way to configure an application, and each of those interfaces then holds — through list(), store(), propertyNames() and toString() — everything the file has, plus everything that was merged into it: the system properties, the environment, the imports. That is what #150 asked about in 2015, having printed one configuration object and got somebody else's keys.

It restricts what is shown and never what is loaded. The distinction is not a nicety: a ${...} in a value is resolved against the other properties, so a configuration that loaded only its own keys could not expand a variable pointing at a key it does not declare — which the reporter worked out for himself, and it is why this is a view and not a load policy. getProperty is left alone for the same reason: asking for a key by name is a question about the file, not about this interface.

The same can be asked of a whole Factory with the owner.declared.only property, which is how a configuration you did not write — one supplied by a plugin, as in the issue — is restricted without annotating it. This annotation wins over that property in both directions: @DeclaredOnly(false) on an interface keeps the whole view when the factory asked for the restriction.

What is declared is every key of every mapping method of this interface and of the interfaces it extends, sections included, under the key each of them actually reads. A method whose key depends on its arguments — @Key("server.%s.host") — has no key until it is called, so nothing of it can be shown; that is the same rule Config.Sensitive and Config.EncryptedValue already follow.

Since:
2.0.0
